newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico says no intervention in peso mkt.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico says no intervention in peso mkt.

text.p: Mexico's central bank said Thursday it did not intervene in the country's foreign exchange market to support the peso, which was badly hit during the day by economic and political concerns.
A Banco de Mexico spokeswoman said the central bank only sells dollar put options to local banks until 1215 p.m. local/1815 GMT, slightly more than an hour before the market closes.
"Since the peso was not more than 2 percent weaker at that time, the Banco de Mexico did not intervene," said the spokeswoman, who wished to remain anonymous.
The peso ended down 17.6 centavos in key 48-hour contracts at 7.96/7.98 per dollar -- more than two percent lower on the day.

Banco de Mexico recently unveiled a plan to build reserves and dampen exchange rate volatility, promising to intervene in the forex market with up to $200 million if the peso falls more than two percent in a given day.

"In case the (dollar) exchange rate rises on a given day by more than two percent from the exchange rate of the previous working day, $200 million will be auctioned among banks with a minimum price two percent above (the exchange rate) on the prior working day," Banco de Mexico said at the time in a statement.
The spokeswoman was unable to say if the central bank would sell dollars at the start of trade on Friday.
